title: Python async (asyncio), Part 8: shutting down and cleaning up
tldr: Every deploy stops the old process: measured on gateway v8, SIGTERM with no handler ends it at once and all 20 shoppers in flight get "connection closed", with nothing logged. The platform side, from the Kubernetes, AWS and Docker docs: SIGTERM, a grace period (30 s by default in Kubernetes, 10 s in docker stop), SIGKILL; a preStop hook spends the same grace period; endpoints are removed while shutdown starts, so a load balancer keeps sending for a while. The tools, traced to CPython 3.14: loop.add_signal_handler (signal.signal left an idle loop asleep until SIGKILL), what asyncio.Runner and asyncio.run do at exit (cancel everything and wait with no limit), async generators whose clean-up runs late and elsewhere, aclose and contextlib.aclosing, and AsyncExitStack. Gateway v9 turns SIGTERM into a timed shutdown in dependency order: stop accepting, drain within a deadline, cancel the rest, wait for single-flight fills, stop seller-e's feed thread, flush the audit queue and metrics; the same deploy answers 25 of 25 and loses no row. Then what breaks: shutdowns that hang (cancels swallowed, open connections, threads), steps in the wrong order, async generators finalized on the wrong loop, signals outside the main thread, on Windows and behind a shell-form CMD, and rollouts at 10 times the load. Ends with drain vs hard stop vs durable handoff, and an interview drill.
